svg.text: K2 — Vessel stack and inversion: how the mechanisms work
Six close-ups, each looping. Orange = moving mechanism (Wender jaws, quill, turntable), steel blue = loose ware, purple = gasket.

g.text: 1 empty pot upside down in jaws B
4 load pins weigh what crossed (±5 g)
The Wender holds the full pot in jaws A, an empty pot upside down
in jaws B, squeezes them together and rolls the pair over.
Only into an empty vessel: additions need the tip cradle.
1 strainer disc clamped on the pot
3 water runs out to the drain
Drain: invert over the rinse seat
A perforated disc is clamped on the pot; the pair is turned over
above the funnel at the foot of the shaft. Hot water never
pours through open air in the room.
1 hot empty pan brought upside down
2 squeezed metal to metal onto the full pan
Pancake, cutlet or patty is flipped by turning the whole pan
over onto a second, preheated pan: 20 s, no turner.
Untested: fat at the metal joint, sticking (risk 2).
The quill pushes food through a cutter disc straight into the
cooking pot, which turns on the K/H turntable. Dicing needs
1–2.5 kN of the 5 kN; 1.5 kg in 90 s. Slicer, grater, ricer alike.
wash: 60 rpm past two jet masts, 55 °C, 120 s
camera check under a stripe light
One load (a pot, or lid and disc) takes 4.5 min: 3 L of reused
liquor, 0.8 L rinse, flash to 105 °C instead of hot rinse
water. Blades and hinged parts go to the central washer.
2 clamp lifts it against the collar
3 cradle rolls: box becomes a hopper
5 rolls back, rest falls into the box
The box itself becomes the hopper: no Wender move per dose.
Granules by shutter, powders by vibrator, liquids and pieces by
roll angle, all closed-loop on a ±1 g scale.
